entries.title: II Chronicles 31:1
segments:
CHAPTER XXXI  
 
 
 
  The people destroy all traces of idolatry throughout Judah, 
   Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh, 1. 
  Hezekiah reforms the state of religion in general; and the 
   tithes are brought in from all quarters, and proper officers 
   set over them, 2-13. 
  They bring to also the freewill-offerings, and regulate the 
   priests and Levites and their families, according to their 
   genealogies, 14-19. 
  Hezekiah does every thing in sincerity and truth, and is 
   prosperous, 20, 21.
 
 NOTES ON CHAP. XXXI 
 
Verse 1. Brake the images in pieces] This species of reformation was not only carried on through Judah, but they carried it into Israel; whether through a transport of religious zeal, or whether with the consent of Hoshea the Israelitish king, we cannot tell.

entries.title: II Chronicles 31:2
segments: Verse 2. In the gates of the tents of the Lord.] That is, in the temple; for this was the house, tabernacle, tent, and camp, of the Most High.

entries.title: II Chronicles 31:3
segments: Verse 3. The king's portion of his substance for the burnt-offerings] It is conjectured that the Jewish kings, at least from the time of David, furnished the morning and evening sacrifice daily at their own expense, and several others also.

entries.title: II Chronicles 31:5
segments: Verse 5. Brought-the first-fruits] These were principally for the maintenance of the priests and Levites; they brought tithes of all the produce of the field, whether commanded or not, as we see in the instance of honey, which was not to be offered to the Lord,
, yet it appears it might be offered to the priests as first-fruits, or in the way of tithes.

entries.title: II Chronicles 31:7
segments:
Verse 7. In the third month] "The month Sivan; the seventh, Tisri."-Targum. 
 
  The heaps] The vast collections of grain which they had from the tithes over and above their own consumption; see

entries.title: II Chronicles 31:11
segments: Verse 11. To prepare chambers] To make granaries to lay up this superabundance.

entries.title: II Chronicles 31:12
segments: Verse 12. Shimei-was the next.] He was assistant to Cononiah.

entries.title: II Chronicles 31:15
segments: Verse 15. And Miniamin] Instead of Nmynm, Miniamin, Nmynb, Benjamin, is the reading of three of Kennicott's and De Rossi's MSS.; and this is the reading of the Vulgate, Syriac, Septuagint, and Arabic.

entries.title: II Chronicles 31:17
segments: Verse 17. From twenty years old] Moses had ordered that the Levites should not begin their labour till they were thirty years of age; but David changed this order, and obliged them to begin at twenty.

entries.title: II Chronicles 31:20
segments: Verse 20. Wrought-good and right and truth] Here is the proper character of a worthy king: he is GOOD, and he does good; he is UPRIGHT, and he acts justly and maintains justice; he is truly RELIGIOUS, and he lives according to that truth which he receives as a revelation from God.

entries.title: II Chronicles 31:21
segments: Verse 21. He did it with all his heart] In every respect he was a thoroughly excellent man, saw his duty to God and to his people, and performed it with becoming zeal and diligence. May God ever send such kings to the nations of the world; and may the people who are blessed with such be duly obedient to them, and thankful to the God who sends them!
